config.title: Generic useFetch<T>

intro.title: Generic useFetch<T>
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable generic composable function called `useFetch<T>` in Vue 3 with TypeScript. This function will fetch data from an API and return it in a type-safe way, allowing you to specify the expected data structure. You will learn how to use TypeScript generics to make the function flexible for different data types while maintaining type safety. The lesson covers key Vue concepts like the Composition API, reactive state with `ref`, and lifecycle hooks. By the end, you'll have a practical utility for handling API requests in your Vue applications.
intro.usecase: The generic useFetch<T> pattern is essential in modern Vue applications that consume multiple API endpoints with consistent data handling. You'll see this in e-commerce dashboards that fetch different product categories, user management systems that retrieve various user profiles, and analytics platforms displaying charts with different data types. This approach allows developers to create a single, type-safe hook that can fetch products, orders, analytics data, or user information while maintaining proper TypeScript inference. It eliminates repetitive fetch logic across components while ensuring each component gets properly typed data for its specific use case.

objectives: Implement a generic TypeScript interface to define the expected structure of a fetch response
Construct a generic Vue composable function that accepts a type parameter for data
Initialize reactive state variables to manage loading status, fetched data, and error messages
Integrate the native fetch API within the composable to retrieve data from a specified URL
Manipulate the component's template to conditionally render loading indicators, data, or errors
Apply the generic useFetch composable in a component with a concrete type to display typed data
Configure the composable to handle different HTTP endpoints and adapt to various data types
